note:
CCSR asks a different question from the published rating. It is a second opinion, not a replacement, and no rating anywhere on this site uses it. ||The model on the rest of this site walks forward through a season and never lets a game inform a prediction made before it. CCSR instead solves for the set of ratings simultaneously consistent with every game at once -- the fixed point of “my rating is my average margin plus my average opponent’s rating”.

The CCSR column below is fitted to the finished season, so it explains that season rather than forecasting it -- which is why it calls a far higher share of winners than the published model does. That gap is hindsight, not skill. The “how it actually scores” panel is the same method refit every week on games through the previous week only, which is the number that can fairly be compared.

The Gap column is not the two ratings subtracted. CCSR is fitted against capped margins and pulled toward a preseason level, so its numbers are spread about 15% more narrowly than the published rating’s; subtracting them straight would rank every strong team as “underrated” and every weak one as “overrated”, which says nothing except that one scale is wider than the other. Gap is what is left once that difference in spread is taken out — so a large one is a real disagreement about a team.
island_note: These teams played nobody outside their own group all season, so how strong they are relative to everyone else is not something the results can answer. ||Their rating comes from their division’s assumed level, not from what they did. Compare them with each other, not with the teams above.
